minutes.headline: Conservation Commission approved three wetland projects and moved to exercise a Chapter 61 right of first refusal.
minutes.summary: The Commission heard notices of intent for a patio and fence at 323 Leominster Road, a dam raising and auxiliary spillway at 164 White Street, and an amended plan at 70 Oak Ridge Road, voting on each. It then went through enforcement items, including unpermitted lake docks that must come in for a request for determination, and signed certificates and orders. A motion on a Chapter 61 right of first refusal was made and seconded.

what_happened.line: The Commission voted to exercise its right of first refusal on a Chapter 61 parcel; the vote was not audible in the captions.
A standard order of conditions was voted for the dam raising and auxiliary spillway at 164 White Street.
Orders of conditions were voted for 323 Leominster Road (patio, fence) and for the amended plan at 70 Oak Ridge Road.
Owners of unpermitted lake docks must file a request for determination and come to a public meeting.
The enforcement order for 307 Townsend Harbor Road gives until January 6 for documentation.

why_it_matters: Exercising a right of first refusal on a Chapter 61 parcel can put forest or farm land into public hands, which would involve town funds and could bring a purchase vote to residents.
The dock requirement and the dam and wetland orders set what property owners near lakes, rivers and wetlands may build and must document.
